The catalog had gone stale by four Actors, and a title change had quietly unrouted two more.

## The catalog was stale, and age was not the signal

`src/catalog.json` described **116** Actors against **120** published. `uflpa-entity-list-monitor`, `bts-db1b-fare-route-market-analytics`, `reg-a-plus-lifecycle-monitor` and `osha-ita-injury-illness-establishment-monitor` were all live on the Store and **invisible to every agent reading this server**.

`check-catalog-live.cjs` is what caught it, and this is precisely why that gate diffs against the live API instead of bounding on age — the catalog that shipped wrong the last time was eight days old. It fired a **second** time in the same session after an unrelated Actor change, catching `blm-solar-siting-area-screener`'s new `simulateOutage` input. Regenerate **after** Actor work, not before.

## Two Actors had silently fallen out of the README

An upstream title change broke the README bucket matcher: `cdfi-nmtc-lowincome-energy-bonus-screener` and `uflpa-entity-list-monitor` matched no bucket and would have been dropped from the documentation entirely.

`gen-readme-coverage.cjs` **reports rather than catch-alls**, so it failed loudly instead of quietly emitting a README missing two Actors — working exactly as designed. Bucket patterns widened to cover both.

The durable lesson: a title change can break a slug- or title-keyed matcher elsewhere in the repo. A generator that swallows an unmatched item hides that; one that fails loudly surfaces it.

## Verification

- `npm test` **63/63**
- mutation harness **23/23 caught**
- `check:catalog` clean against the live API — 120 Actors, matched

**Catalog** 116 → 120 Actors.
